articles.title: Who is Manisha Bhanwala? The Emotional Story Behind India's First Woman Wrestling ...
articles.content: Manisha Bhanwala created history by becoming the first ever Indian woman wrestler to win a Senior World Wrestling Championships title. The 29-year-old wrestler from Haryana achieved this milestone on Friday, October 30, after defeating American opponent Abigail Nette in the women's 59kg freestyle final. In the finals, she made a stunning comeback after trailing 0-6 to eventually win the match by 8-6. The championship is taking place in Astana, Kazakhstan. How did Manisha Bhanwala defeat Abigail Nette in the final? America's Abigail Nette secured a 4-point lead in the early stages of the match. Manisha initially challenged a decision but her challenge was unsuccessful giving Abigail 1 point more. Then she went on to extend the lead to 6-0. Manisha then made her comeback by scoring her first point through a step out. She followed it with a brilliant move to level the score at 6-6. In the final stages of the match, she executed another takedown to take an 8-6 lead. She maintained her advantage until the final whistle, entering the history books with a historic World Championships gold medal. Manisha Bhanwala was born in Siwaha village in Jind district of Haryana on February 10, 1997. She started her journey in fitness and weight management. Her elder brother also inspired her interest in sports. Eventually she joined the Sir Chhotu Ram Wrestling Academy in Rohtak. She competed across different weight categories before developing into an international level wrestler. The Emotional Toll that Shaped Manisha Bhanwala's Career One of the most heartbreaking moments in Manisha Bhanwala's life came in 2022 when her father passed away. He had encouraged her to take up wrestling and supported her journey as a sportsperson. He passed away just hours before Manisha was about to travel to Mongolia for the Senior Asian Wrestling Championships. She was deeply affected by her father's death and eventually decided to quit wrestling. However her family members encouraged her to continue wrestling and fulfil her father's dream. Manisha eventually travelled to Mongolia and won a bronze medal at the 2022 Asian Wrestling Championships. Now she has fulfilled her father's dream in 2026 after winning the gold medal at the Senior World Wrestling Championships. articles.title: ISRO Successfully Launches NVS-03 Satellite Aboard GSLV-F18… - The Open Press
articles.content: India ISRO Successfully Launches NVS-03 Satellite Aboard GSLV-F18, Strengthening India’s NavIC Navigation System The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has achieved another significant milestone in the country’s space programme with the successful launch of its next-generation navigation satellite, NVS-0… Published By : Neeraj Singh , Sriharikota Last Updated: October 31, 2026, 09:47 IST ISRO's GSLV-F18 rocket lifts off from Sriharikota carrying the NVS-03 next-generation navigation satellite. The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has achieved another significant milestone in the country’s space programme with the successful launch of its next-generation navigation satellite, NVS-03. The satellite was launched aboard the GSLV-F18 rocket from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota at 11:51 pm on October 30, 2026. The mission is an important step towards strengthening India’s indigenous satellite navigation system, Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), and ensuring continuity of its navigation services. The 50-metre-tall, three-stage launch vehicle, with a lift-off mass of approximately 420 tonnes, carried the 2,232-kg NVS-03 satellite. The spacecraft was successfully placed into its intended Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO) approximately 18 minutes and 40 seconds after lift-off. GSLV Completes Its 20th Flight The GSLV-F18 mission marked the 20th flight of India's Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle programme. It was also ISRO's third space launch of 2026. Following its placement in the transfer orbit, NVS-03 will undergo further orbital manoeuvres using its onboard thrusters to reach its designated geosynchronous orbital position at approximately 32.5 degrees East. The successful launch marks another step in India's efforts to strengthen its independent satellite navigation infrastructure. Read More: ISRO Successfully Launches EOS-05, Strengthening India’s Earth Observation Capabilities What Is NavIC and Why Does India Need It? NavIC, or Navigation with Indian Constellation, is India's indigenous satellite-based navigation system. It is designed to provide positioning, navigation and timing services across the Indian landmass and an area extending approximately 1,500 kilometres beyond the country's boundaries. The system provides India with an independent navigation capability rather than relying entirely on foreign satellite navigation networks. Its applications include transportation, maritime operations, emergency services, disaster management and strategic requirements. Indigenous Atomic Clock and New L1 Signal Make NVS-03 Special One of the key features of NVS-03 is its indigenous atomic clock, which is carried alongside procured atomic clocks. Highly accurate timekeeping is essential for satellite navigation because positioning calculations depend on precisely measuring the time taken by signals to travel between satellites and receivers. The satellite also introduces the L1 frequency signal in addition to NavIC's existing L5 and S-band signals. This addition is expected to enhance the system's capabilities and improve compatibility with a wider range of navigation receivers. However, wider use in smartphones and other consumer devices will depend on the satellite's operational readiness, service availability and support from device manufacturers. articles.title: Western Ghats on wheels soon: Karnataka to launch India's first mobile biodiversity museum
articles.content: BENGALURU: The Karnataka government will soon launch India’s first Western Ghats on Wheels- a mobile museum showcasing the endemic and unique biodiversity of the biodiversity hotspot. The specially designed Volvo bus will travel around the state, catering to various sections of society. Karnataka State Western Ghats Taskforce Committee Chairman Mohammed Tabrez Alam Shariff said, the state has approved the bus and it will be launched in another six months. The estimated budget for the project is Rs1 crore. Volvo is donating a 15metre 9600 service model multi-axle luxury coach for the mobile museum. Interactive and holographic screens will be placed inside the bus showcasing wildlife, waterfalls and forests. The bus will operate on roof mounted solar panels and zero-carbon footprint, he said. The bus will be divided into three sections, the two sides will be used as two corridors, occupying three-fourth of the bus for display. The remaining portion will be utilised as the seating area for discussions. Theme based life-size models are also planned to be displayed inside the bus. Shariff said, images and videos for creating the virtual videos and for display will be sources for multiple sources. Graphics and animations will also be used for drawing the attention of children. Theme based forests will also be created inside the bus which can be changed. Shariff said, discussions are also on to create a dedicated immobile Western Ghats museum spread across 10acre of land in Jarakabanade reserve forest, near HMT. Land for the project is awaited and work is likely to start after another six months. With this Western Ghats experience centres will also be set up in various parts of the state, he added.
